fills.researcher_notes: Existing ref (eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php#pipelines, a generic nav page) is live but names no status token and doesn't name the project -- replaced with better sources. EIA's own Natural Gas Pipeline Projects dataset has tracked this project as 'Completed' (completed_date 2021-03-01) continuously across every release from 2021-07 through the current 2026-08 release (22 releases spanning 6+ years, several dated well after the sheet's 2025-09-18 LastUpdated) -- no reversal, no re-designation. Boardwalk's own subsidiary page independently lists Gulf South Pipeline Company as a currently operating interstate system. Two independent origins (EIA + Boardwalk) agree: operating is correct, unchanged.

Existing ref is live but the pipeline name isn't found on that generic nav page. This project is listed in EIA's 'Natural Gas Pipeline Projects' dataset (a natural-gas-only dataset by definition) and the FERC Federal Register notice describes it as a request under the Natural Gas Act to increase certificated capacity by '48,000 dekatherms per day' of natural gas at Gulf South's McComb Compressor Station -- two independent agencies (EIA, FERC) both confirm this is a natural gas facility.

Neither source uses the verbatim word 'transmission,' so this is a regulatory-jurisdiction inference rather than a direct label match (hence medium, not high). The Federal Register notice describes the compressor station as part of Gulf South's 'Index 130 mainline' and the request is made under FERC's Natural Gas Act blanket-certificate authority (18 CFR 157.205 etc.) -- FERC/NGA jurisdiction reaches only interstate TRANSMISSION facilities, not local distribution (state-regulated) or gathering (largely unregulated). EIA's own dataset independently tags this project 'Pipeline Type: Interstate', 'Authority: FERC', docket CP20-32 -- consistent with a transmission-system compressor station, not a distribution or gathering asset.

Federal Register notice states explicitly: 'Take notice that on December 20, 2019, Gulf South Pipeline Company, LP...filed a prior notice application' for this project (docket CP20-32). EIA's January 2020 dataset release (a separate agency, last_updated_date on this row = 2020-01-08) already lists the project with status 'Applied' -- consistent with, and independent corroboration of, a December 2019 filing date. ProposalYear=2019/ProposalMonth=12 was previously blank; this is a new fill, not a change to an existing value.

EIA's January 2021 dataset release records this project's status as 'Construction' (row last_updated_date = 2020-06-26), placing construction underway by mid-2020, ahead of the March 2021 completion. Single-origin (EIA only) -- searched FERC's own monthly Energy Infrastructure Update reports for mid/late-2020 for an independent second source pinpointing a construction-start date; only the December 2019 EIU (pre-construction, proposal-stage) is available in this batch's source cache, and FERC's EIU/news-listing pages 403'd on re-fetch. No month-level granularity found anywhere; leaving ConstructionMonth blank rather than guessing. Tier medium given the single confirmed origin.

Sheet already records StartYear1=2021 with no ref (MISSING_REF). EIA's July 2021 release first records completed_date=2021-03-01 for this project; every subsequent release through 2026-08 (22 releases total) repeats the identical date, unrevised for 5+ years. Confirms StartYear1=2021 and additionally pins the month (March). All corroboration traces to one origin (EIA) -- searched for an independent FERC in-service notice for March/April 2021 (FERC's EIU listing page and monthly-update pages 403'd on this pass); tier medium reflects single-origin, high-persistence evidence rather than two independent origins. Adding StartMonth1=3 as a new, previously-blank data point.

EIA's own snapshots document a genuine ~1-year schedule slip: the January 2020 release (Applied/Construction-stage) carries 'Year In Service Date = 2020', while the actual completed_date first reported in July 2021 is 2021-03-01 -- i.e., the project slipped from an expected 2020 in-service date to March 2021. No press release or FERC filing formally announces a 'delay' (hence DelayType=inferred is the correct tag, not 'confirmed' -- there is no company/regulator statement using the word delay). Confirms the sheet's existing Delayed=yes/DelayType=inferred values are well-supported, not merely uncontested.

Three sources agree, from two independent agencies: FERC's own December 2019 Energy Infrastructure Update states verbatim 'The project would result in 48 MMcf/d of increased capacity on its system.' The Federal Register notice states the increase as '48,000 dekatherms per day (Dth/d)' (Dth/d and MMcf/d are used near-interchangeably for pipeline-quality gas in these FERC filings). EIA's dataset independently records additional_capacity_mmcf_d=48 across all 22 tracked releases 2020-2026. Confirms the sheet's existing 48.00 MMcf/d exactly.

No source found stating an operating/MAOP pressure for the McComb Compressor Station specifically. Searched: the Federal Register notice (describes compressor horsepower -- a new 8,565 HP unit replacing three existing reciprocating compressors -- but no pressure rating), FERC's December 2019 EIU, and EIA's dataset (no pressure field). This is a compressor-station reliability/efficiency project, not a new pipeline segment with a stated design pressure; leaving blank rather than guessing.

Confirms LengthKnown=0 is the correct, intentional value for this row per the batch's scope rule: this is a compressor-station upgrade (new compressor installed, three retired) with no new pipe laid. The Federal Register notice describes only compressor work at an existing station site in Walthall County; EIA's dataset carries no mileage value for this project across any of its 22 tracked releases (Miles field is blank in every release, including the current live workbook). Nothing to fix -- Diameter blank (see below) follows from the same fact.

Diameter blank is the CORRECT, intentional state per this batch's scope rule for LengthKnown=0 compression-only rows -- there is no new pipe segment to have a diameter. EIA's own 'Pipeline Diameter (Inches)' field is blank for this project across every one of its 22 tracked releases (2020-01 through 2026-08), which is itself corroborating: even EIA, tracking the same project with a dedicated diameter column, records nothing. Not a data gap to fix.

No source specifies what fuels the new 8,565 HP compressor unit (electric-drive vs. gas-fired reciprocating/turbine) at McComb. The Federal Register notice describes the unit only as a replacement for 'three existing reciprocating gas compressors' -- suggestive but not a direct statement that the NEW unit is also gas-fired. Searched FERC's Dec 2019 EIU and EIA's dataset; neither states a fuel source for the driver. Leaving blank rather than inferring from the retired units' fuel type.

Federal Register notice: the McComb Compressor Station is 'located on Gulf South's Index 130 mainline in Walthall County, Mississippi.' EIA's dataset independently records State(s)='MS' for every one of its 22 tracked releases. Two independent agencies agree; confirms Mississippi/United States for both start and end (single-point compressor-station project, not a linear route).

No cost figure found for this project. EIA's own 'Cost (millions)' field is blank for this project across all 22 tracked releases (2020-01 through 2026-08) -- EIA itself, which tracks cost for many other projects in the same dataset, has no figure here either. The Federal Register notice (a prior-notice/blanket-authorization filing, not a certificate application) does not require or include a cost estimate. Searched FERC's Dec 2019 EIU (no cost given) and general web search for any trade-press cost estimate for this small compressor-reliability project; none found. Leaving blank.
